for m in re.finditer(r'"content":\[(.*?)\]', t, re.DOTALL):
    content_str = m.group(1)
    
    lines = content_str.replace('\\n', '\n').split('\n')
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.match(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \(\d+x\d+\):\n?', line):
            match = re.match(r'(.+) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n?', line)
            if match:
                name, h, w = match.group(1), int(match.group(2)), int(match.group(3))
                
                rows = []
                j = i + 1
                while len(rows) < h and j < len(lines):
                    row_line = lines[j].strip()
                    if re.match(r'^\d+\s+\d+', row_line):
                        parts = [int(x) for x in row_line.split()]
                        if len(parts) == w:
                            rows.append(parts)
                        else:

                    j += 1
                
                if rows and all(len(r) == w for r in rows):
                    G[name] = rows

# Parse the grids directly from the JSONL using the raw text pattern I found
import json, os, re

d = os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
filepath = d + '/../../sessions/01a18a10-9b41-757a-8f6f-ccf1ce6a2959.jsonl'

with open(filepath) as f:
    content = f.read()

pattern = r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n(Demo pair|\n\n|\z))'

matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content))

    grids[name] = rows
